title: Entra ID Privilege Escalation

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:auditlog` events with `activityDisplayName="Add member to role"` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.3 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:auditlog` traffic without `activityDisplayName="Add member to role"`. Confirm UC-4.2.3 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:auditlog` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:auditlog" activityDisplayName="Add member to role"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.3_entra_id_privilege_escal_3"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.2.3 — Entra ID Privilege Escalation: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:auditlog` for search criteria `activityDisplayName="Add member to role"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Entra ID Privilege Escalation' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.3 drives critical-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.

knownFalsePositives: Some risky scores come from new devices, working from home, or a partner logging in the same way we do. We do not want every medium flag to page us; we pair higher scores with new locations, odd hours, or multiple clouds before we act.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:auditlog`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Forward Entra ID audit logs. Create critical alerts on role assignments for Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator, and Exchange Administrator. Correlate with PIM activation events.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:auditlog" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:auditlog" activityDisplayName="Add member to role"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.3_entra_id_privilege_escal_3"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:auditlog` in `index=azure` to detect entra id privilege escalation. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_3_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Events list (critical), Table (who assigned what to whom), Timeline..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of entra id privilege escalation so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
